output.brief:
The rise in missed appointments is real and tied to the Tidewell change. Four findings support this. Eastgate, still on the old system, is flat at about 8%, so the bus cut and seasonal effects don't explain it. Corrie Lane was also about 8% a year earlier. A clinical audit found miscoded records account for only about 0.5 points of the rise, so the recording explanation is minor. Front-desk calls were never stopped. They only covered the minor-procedures list, so blaming and warning staff is unsupported and would be harmful.

Two Tidewell changes happened on the same day. Reminders moved from 48 hours to 7 days, and the booking horizon grew from about 19 to about 52 days. Patient comments point to the reminder, but the evidence can't separate it from the longer wait. No data links lead time or message timing to outcomes, and the vendor quotes 10 weeks for the extract.

I'm fairly sure about what it isn't. I'm unsure which Tidewell change matters more, or whether both do.

Next steps: run the randomised 48-hour reminder test on half the templates. Request the lead-time extract now. Keep reporting the DNA rate to the board, with a note about the 0.5-point miscoding effect. Don't discipline staff.
